title: Light Potting Soil, Suitable for Succulents
text:
Light Potting Soil, Suitable for Succulents. This ORGANIC POTTING SOIL (Fast Draining Cactus and Succulent Soil Mix; 4 Quarts) is advertised as a “professional growing mix”, and I’m not qualified to challenge that statement. I do know that cacti and succulents grow better in lightweight or sandy soil that is designed to drain quickly and provide the correct Ph balance. This potting soil seems perfectly fine for my succulents. (I'm not sure whether you need to add additional fertilizer, once your plants are rooted.)

However, the potting soil is very expensive (about $10 on Amazon for a 4-quart package). Think about the volume of 1-gallon milk jug. That is approximately the amount of soil you receive in 4 dry quarts. This amount will allow you to plant a lot of little succulents in 3” starter pots or cells. However, it will fill only a couple of 6” houseplant pots.

If you need cactus/succulent potting mix on a regular basis, you can save money by purchasing it in 8-quart or larger bags (e.g., [[ASIN:B08DHDLRYN Hoffman cactus and succulent potting soil]]). Also, local nurseries generally carry potting soil for many specialized uses (e.g., cacti, palms, African violets, orchids), and their prices are usually lower than those of online sellers.
